messages.subject: modification to assignment 3 collocation code
parts:
Hello,

While I am working through Qclwr I am also wanting to jump ahead and
employ the collocation code in Assignment 3.

The data I want to analyse consists of a csv file with 159 rows (1 row
per person x up to 16 columns of data - average = 8 columns of text).
An example of a single cell follows:

There appears an increase in his general level of risk. This should be
treated seriously. If his biological treatment is considered optimal,
then attention is required to his psychosocial functioning (e.g coping
skills and conflict resolution skills).

I changed the input file into my csv file and the code ran without
error, however there was no output - see following output:

[1] a.s b.s c.s d.s expa.s relation.s
mi.s chi.s
<0 rows> (or 0-length row.names)

I am considering two potential reasons for this outcome:

1) the data is not being read in correctly at the scan stage (see
following original code),

current.file<-tolower(scan(corpus.file, what="char", sep="\n",
quote="", quiet=T)) # read in data

2) the data has been read as a non-sentence and filtered (see
following original code).

tagged.corpus.sentences<-grep("<s n=", current.file, value=T) #
filter out non-sentences

I am interested in suggestions as to possible ways to resolve this.
For example, should I try to alter the scan command or the data file
(e.g concatenate the columns so there is only one column per person)
or remove the tagged.corpus.sentences command. I tried the latter and
substituted 'tagged.corpus.sentences' for 'current.file' below
however, the result was again no output.

# compile the frequency list
current.words.1<-unlist(strsplit(tagged.corpus.sentences, "\\W*<.*?
>", perl=T)) # split up the lines into words


Any suggestions are much appreciated,

Bob

messages.author: 3edc58ee737edd94
messages.subject: Re: modification to assignment 3 collocation code
parts: > If I run it without (because I don't have the "<s n=" string)
Right, that's of course what you need to do!

> I am unsure how to edit the line below because 'tagged.corpus.sentences' doesn't exist. I tried inserting current.file but this did not produce any results.
> current.words.1<-unlist(strsplit(tagged.corpus.sentences, "\\W*<.*?>", perl=T)) # split up the lines into words

Well, it's hard to say without a specific example, but

(i) at least based on the script file for assignment 3,
current.corpus.file would be the most promising candidate, or of
course whatever you call the file you read;
(ii) of course, this line doesn't yield results when you apply it to
your text file if, as I dare assume, your file doesn't have BNC-style
SGML tags that match "<.*?>" ... ;-) You need to change the line to
what you want to use; the sections on frequency lists and collocations
in the book provide examples.

Cheers,
STG
--
Stefan Th. Gries

University of California, Santa Barbara
